subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Which provider-error classes may be retried during a locked OAuth refresh, and what maximum lock-held latency is acceptable before the existing fallback/error path must run?
rationale: The correct classifier varies by provider and token-rotation behavior; an unconditional generic retry would alter authentication failure semantics and contention behavior for existing deployments.

options.title: Adopt a narrow shared transient classifier
options.body: Retry only clearly transient transport, timeout, and selected 5xx/rate-limit failures with a short bounded budget, while never retrying terminal OAuth failures.

options.title: Keep single-shot refresh
options.body: Retain the current lock, adoption, and fallback behavior until provider-specific retry contracts are defined.

options.title: Define provider-owned policies
options.body: Let each provider/plugin explicitly opt into retryable refresh errors, trading a clearer contract for more implementation work.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow shared transient classifier
recommendation.body: Retry only clearly transient transport, timeout, and selected 5xx/rate-limit failures with a short bounded budget, while never retrying terminal OAuth failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The central OAuth-manager lifecycle and refresh flow are most closely tied to this history.
